dharana.numbering_edition: Jaideva Singh 1979 (dhāraṇā 1 = verse 24; dhāraṇā 82 = verses 105–106 and dhāraṇā 89 = verses 113–114, otherwise one verse each; dhāraṇā 112 = verse 137)
dharana.sanskrit_iast: sarvatra bhairavo bhāvaḥ sāmānyeṣv api gocaraḥ | na ca tadvyatirekeṇa paro 'stīty advayā gatiḥ ||
dharana.sanskrit_source: GRETIL e-text, compared with Wallis's concordance, Pradīpaka and the Singh scan
sanskrit_variants: verse 124: GRETIL (and Pradīpaka) read -vyatirekteṇa; corrected to -vyatirekeṇa with Wallis.
dharana.rendering: The state of Bhairava is everywhere, within reach even of ordinary people; 'there is nothing other than That': one who knows this has the non-dual path.
dharana.rendering_attribution: School paraphrase drawing on Jaideva Singh (1979), Christopher Wallis and Bettina Bäumer (as printed in Wallis's concordance); not a quotation.
dharana.commentary_note: Singh: this dhāraṇā needs no particular meditation practice. Everyone, even the unlearned, knows the 'I'; the everyday 'I' is a symbol of the eternal 'I' throbbing in every heart, consciousness-bliss, which is Bhairava, known within; and He is known outwardly through His manifestation in the cosmos. He cites Maheśvarānanda's Mahārthamañjarī (verse 4) and calls this an example of anupāya, the 'means without means'. Wallis: 'the Bhairava state'.
dharana.technique_name: Bhairava Is Everywhere, Even in the Ordinary
dharana.instruction: Recognise the plain sense 'I am', and the ordinary world around you, as the sacred itself.

checked_against: The Mystery Within (2019), Session Two list: 'Dharana 99' = verse 124 (agrees with Singh)
Wallis concordance: verse 124 = 'The Bhairava state (Y99 ~ B3)' (verse text and technique match)
GRETIL, Wallis and Pradīpaka: Sanskrit of verse 124 compared
verification.notes: Door index = Singh dhāraṇā number, read directly in Singh's own headings and cross-checked against The Mystery Within's Singh-numbered list and Wallis's concordance. Caveat: Singh was read from an OCR scan, not a print copy in hand.

numbering_variants.mystery_within_parallel: The parallel-translations section of The Mystery Within labels verse 124 'Dharana 101', because from verse 106 on it gives every verse its own number (106 = 83 … 137 = 114). Singh and the same book's Session Two list put this at dhāraṇā 99. Not followed.

seat.label: Any steady, comfortable position (school addition)
seat.summary: Any steady, comfortable position: sitting on a chair, sitting on the floor with support under the hips, or lying on the back. Standing or walking slowly is also acceptable when that is easier. Choose the position in which the body needs the least effort.
seat.honesty: School addition. Verse 124 does not specify a body position. The seat is a convenience so the dharana can be practised; it is not part of the technique and makes no claim of tradition.

points: the simple sense 'I am' everyone has
geometry.summary: Not a body shape. The map is the plainest sense of 'I am', shared by everyone, and the whole world, with nothing outside them.
geometry.svg_hint: a plain everyday scene with a soft light present in every part of it
geometry.honesty: Geometry records the dharana's own map of attention, not a body shape. Locations marked 'commentarial' come from commentary, not from the verse.

reaction.name: Nothing apart
reaction.summary: School metaphor only: the sacred stops being somewhere special and is recognised in the plainest, most ordinary experience. Not a biochemical or medical claim.

breath.lands_in: wherever the breath naturally ends; this door places nothing on the breath
breath.cue: Natural breath. Count about four in and four out only if it helps you settle, then let the count go. No forced hold.
breath.honesty: The counts are an optional school pacing aid, not part of the verse. Hold is always 0: this school never adds a deliberate breath-hold.

orientation.cue: Turn attention toward what the verse names, and let everything else stay in the background
orientation.gravity: Let the floor or chair carry the body completely; there is no posture to hold
orientation.degrees_hint: No angle target: the VBT gives no posture for this dharana

attention.primary: The plain sense 'I am', present in everyone
attention.secondary: The recognition that there is nothing apart from it

adiyogi.verse_paraphrase: The state of Bhairava is everywhere, within reach even of ordinary people; 'there is nothing other than That': one who knows this has the non-dual path.
adiyogi.method_summary: No technique is needed. Notice the plain sense 'I am' that everyone has, and the ordinary world around you. Recognise both as That, with nothing apart from it.

honesty.disclosure: Door 099 follows Vijñāna Bhairava Tantra dharana 99 (verse 124) in Jaideva Singh's numbering. The door-to-dharana index is a School of 112 Doorways teaching device. Singh's sequence is one edition's count, not an ancient one-to-one canon. The seat, counts, reaction and beat scripts are school additions.
honesty.notes: pairing_type is school_device: the dharana is the content, while the door index, seat and pacing are the school's.
flags: Door index = Jaideva Singh dharana number: Door 099 is dharana 99, verse 124. Other editions number differently (see dharana.numbering_variants).
The seat, breath counts, reaction metaphor, attention-map drawing and beat scripts are school devices, not part of the verse.
The English is a school paraphrase, not a quotation from any translator.
No medical claims. Reaction names are metaphors, not biochemistry.

safety.pain_rule: Pain is information. Pause, regress, or exit. Never push through sharp pain.
safety.open_seat_alternate: This door needs no particular posture: sit on a chair, sit on the floor with support, or lie down. Eyes may stay open.
safety.contraindication_notes: General practice caution only; not medical advice. Nothing to achieve here; if it feels abstract, simply rest. If anything feels distressing (dizziness, agitation, strong emotion), stop, open the eyes and rest attention on the feet and the floor.
